Holyoke Conservation Commission Meeting 
Minutes 8/13/26 
Conservation Commission Members Present: Jeffery Horan (Chairperson), Mary Moriarty (Vice Chairperson), 
Patricia Normand, John Perdrizet, Bernice Bowler, Rosemary Arnold, Michael Dodge 
Conservation Commission Members Absent: None 
Staff Present: Maggie Herlihy (Conservation Planner) 
Members of the Public Present: Joey Pellegrino, Randy Reynolds, Sara Berryman (VHB), Alan Kwasnik (HG&E), 
Sean Mullen 
 
1. Call to Order 
Chairperson Horan called the meeting to order at 6:15 p.m.   
 
2. Enforcement Order – Continued from 7/6/26 
Location: 5 Appleton Street (MBP: 049-01-006) 
Description: Grading and fill deposition along approximately 470 lineal feet of banks within Riverfront, Banks, and 
Priority and Estimated Habitats of Rare Species associated with the Connecticut River. Fill sediments and 
associated debris were observed eroding down the steep bank towards the water. 
 
Chairperson Horan asked Randy Reynolds whether the soil testing results had been received, and Mr. Reynolds 
confirmed that they had.   
 
Sara Berryman of VHB presented the draft restoration plan.  She shared a very detailed map of the area and 
explained that the plan called for selective removal of excess sediment from two work areas, smoothing and 
regrading other affected areas to reduce the steep drop-off, and applying an erosion-control seed mix for 
stabilization.  The plan also included a construction entrance with a tracking pad, a silt sack in the nearby catch 
basin, repair or reinstallation of existing silt fence where it was not making adequate contact with the ground, and 
installation of an additional silt fence closer to the building to slow runoff and prevent additional sediment from 
moving toward the river. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty asked about the soil testing, with regards reported heavy metals and a small amount of 
asbestos in one of the sampled areas.  Ms. Berryman stated that, as a wetland scientist, she could not provide a 
contamination determination and that VHB’s Licensed Site Professional had not yet completed review of the 
recently received results. 
 
Mr. Reynolds stated that he had not previously been advised of the positive asbestos result, but noted that his 
company also performs asbestos abatement and could address the situation if necessary.  He further explained that 
the contamination/remediation work would need to be identified and completed before the final restoration and 
seeding work.
Page 2 of 6 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty also inquired about the silt fence up near the building and how long it would have to be 
there.  Ms. Berryman explained its purpose would be to contain the soils near the building and prevent their being 
washed down the hill toward the river during rainstorms and that it would ideally be removed sometime during 
growing season in 2027.  Chairperson Horan expressed the need for a clear plan that communicates the sequencing 
of the contamination response and restoration work.  VHB’s Berryman asked if the asbestos removal should be 
included in the plan sequencing. Mr. Reynolds expressed that he would have to check where the asbestos is.  Mr. 
Reynolds mentioned his recent communications with HG&E and Pinsly Railroad about their work in the area, 
stressing the importance of all parties being clear about plans for the area. 
Conservation Agent Herlihy reminded the Commission  that  Natural Heritage (NHESP) must be involved for this 
location. 
Alan Kwasnik from HG&E spoke about collaboration with American Environmental to remove a large amount of 
trash from the area.  Chairperson Horan asked Mr. Kwasnik if he had a chance to review the plan, and Mr. Kwasnik 
answered saying that this was not his forte, but spoke on the power line work in the area and noted Pinsly's plan to 
redo the rail.  He commented that the Commission's plan seems very reasonable.  Chairperson Horan asked him if 
there will be an annual maintenance plan, and Mr. Kwasnik said that they try to keep the vegetation down by 
cutting it two to four times a year.  Ms. Berryman added that there's no proposal of planting trees or shrubs, aiming 
to keep the plants on the site low-growing. 
Vice-Chair Moriarty asked if it is safe to say that this plan is fine with HG&E.  Alan Kwasnik from HG&E said “yes it 
is.” 
 
The Commission clarified that the entities involved include HG&E, Pinsly Railroad and Natural Heritage.  
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty asked how the plan will be submitted.  Ms. Berryman said that they haven't submitted it 
on their end but that they can prepare it and do so.   Vice Chairperson Moriarty  recapped the steps in the plan .She 
asked if the steps in the plan would be: first, all of the information would be sent to Natural Heritage and Pinsly, 
then, the silt fence will be put in place as a temporary measure, and then the soil remediation will occur.   
Chairperson Horan verified the plan and asked Ms. Berryman to add a sequence to make all the steps clear. 
Chairperson Horan clarified that the silt fence could be added first and the seeding will take place after the 
remediation. Ms. Berryman agreed to do so.   
Conservation Agent Herlihy asked for clarification if the Commission was asking to approve the remediation plan 
before any additional work occurs.  Chairperson Horan said we have to because it is part of the final close-out of 
the enforcement order and is related to the seeding plan. 
 
Chairperson Horan expressed that the order cannot be approved at the present time, and Ms. Herlihy added that 
the soil remediation plan would have to be approved at least, and then the entire restoration plan needs to be 
approved by Natural Heritage and Pinsly. Chairperson Horan asked how long it will take to come up with a 
remediation plan. Mr. Reynolds said that a remediation plan shouldn't take very long.  He expressed his willingness 
to install the silt fences in time for the August 27th Conservation Commission meeting.  Chairperson Horan advised 
the representatives that they did not need to appear at the August 27 meeting if the required information was not 
yet complete, but that they should continue providing progress updates to Ms. Herlihy. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty moved to continue the order to the August 27 meeting, and Commissioner Dodge 
seconded the motion.  The motion was approved unanimously, 7-0. 
 
Chairperson Horan acknowledged the presence of Conservation Agent Elect Joey Pellegrino and Conservation
Page 3 of 6 
 
Planner Applicant Sean Mullen. 
 
3. Draft Priority Habitat Map of Rare Species Available for Public Comment 
Ms. Herlihy presented the draft Priority Habitat of Rare Species map that was open for public comment through 
October 4th.  She compared the current and proposed maps and identified the expansion of priority habitat areas in 
various areas including Mount Tom, Mountain Park, Holyoke Community College, Wyckoff, the Log Cabin, McLean 
Reservoir and Ashley Reservoir. 
 
She clarified that the revisions reflect changes to the Massachusetts Endangered Species Act list, new species 
occurrences, removal of historic occurrences more than twenty-five years old, newer biological research, 
regulatory review outcomes, improved aerial photography, GIS data, and exclusion of sites with poor estimated 
population viability.  Commissioner Arnold asked whether the vernal pool on the Gloutak property or the pond on 
West Cherry Street are included, and Ms. Herlihy confirmed that they are.  
 
Chairperson Horan asked for a motion to have Agent Herlihy submit comments on our behalf saying the Holyoke 
Conservation Commission has reviewed the habitat map and concurs with the changes.  Commissioner Arnold 
made a motion to that affect. Commissioner Normand seconded the motion.  The motion was approved 
unanimously, 6-0, with Michael Dodge being absent at the time of the vote.  
 
4. Discussion – Temporary Ad-Hoc Committee to Study and Provide an Analysis on the 
Potential Impacts of Commercial Data Center Development in Holyoke 
 
The Commission reviewed updated language from the City for the proposed committee with regards to the rules 
about the membership consisting of representatives from various entities.  They discussed whether the 
Conservation Commission representative should be limited to a Commissioner or whether the language should be 
updated to allow a member of the Conservation Department to serve, similar to language used for some other City 
boards and departments. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty suggested that having more than one member from the Conservation Commission may 
be appreciate in a sort of "tag team" arrangement due to the large commitment required by the committee.  
Chairperson Horan acknowledged that the arrangement makes sense for the Conservation Commission but may 
cause issues with the cohesion of the ad-hoc committee. He mentioned that the size of the ad-hoc committee and 
who will be represented is being worked out by City Council. He also commented on the lack of any staffing for the 
committee which he believed would cause problems.  No commissioners volunteered during the meeting, but 
Chairperson Horan encouraged them to think about it. 
 
5. Discussion – PILOT Listening Session 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty and Commissioner Arnold reported on the state Payment in Lieu of Taxes (PILOT) 
listening session they attended.  The discussion focused on concerns that the current PILOT system can create 
inequalities between communities, particularly where state-owned conservation land removes property from local 
tax rolls but the municipality receives comparatively limited reimbursement. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty summarized discussion at the listening session concerning the state’s 30-by-30 land
Page 4 of 6 
 
conservation goals, differences in land values across Massachusetts, and the limited statewide funding available for 
PILOT payments.  Commissioner Arnold noted that participants in her group discussed the fiscal impact of land 
that has been removed from the tax rolls and the importance of acknowledging the municipal contribution when 
land is protected for statewide conservation purposes. 
Ms. Herlihy reviewed Holyoke properties that may or may not currently be included in the PILOT calculation and 
discussed ongoing work with the Assessor’s Office to understand the relevant land-use codes and the basis for 
inclusion.  She expressed the importance of being consistent with the categorization of parcels.  She informs that 
she is currently waiting to hear back from the Holyoke Assessor's Office on their findings. She mentioned that only 
assessor’s offices can communicate with each other, so, she could not reach out to the state assessor to inquire 
about discrepancies. She had spoken to one DCR representative who said that they can present this as a case study 
to the committee, though Holyoke's situation is unlikely to change.   
Commissioner Arnold commented on the properties taken by eminent domain by the State, discussing with Ms. 
Herlihy the fact that Holyoke has not been reimbursed even though those properties would have been on the tax 
roll. Commissioner Arnold also suggested exploring whether some form of payment could be associated with the 
Edna Williams property before future City Council action.  Ms. Herlihy reported that a meeting with Fish and Game 
was being planned to discuss that property.  
 
6. Discussion – Reauthorization to Purchase iPads 
Ms. Herlihy reported that her office had been broken into while on vacation, and that iPads and two laptops had 
been stolen.  She gave an update regarding efforts to locate the missing items, confirming that cell service to the 
iPads had been shut off.  The Commission was to discuss whether to authorize the purchase of two iPads, two 
Apple Pencils and two iPad cases to replace the stolen items.  Ms. Herlihy and Chairperson Horan discussed how 
the replacement items would cost and how the purchases would be funded. Chairperson Horan believed that an 
authorization of $1,000 would be appropriate, with the understanding that the actual expense may be significantly 
lower. 
 
Commissioner Bowler made a motion to authorize up to $1,000 for the purchase of replacement iPads and related 
equipment, using the operational budget and an appropriate component of wetland permitting-fee funds. 
Commissioner John Perdrizet seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously 6-0, with Michael Dodge 
being absent at the time of the vote.   The Commission also discussed whether a protection plan such as AppleCare 
should be purchased with the replacement devices, noting that AppleCare could provide theft and damage 
coverage but would require a monthly expense.  Chairperson Horan suggested talking to Jamie to find out how 
difficult that might be. 
 
7. Discussion – Hiring of Conservation Planner 
The Commission discussed the open Conservation Planner position.  The application period was scheduled to close 
on August 17, and approximately ten applications had been received, with roughly eight appearing qualified at the 
time of the meeting.  The Chair stated that at least four candidates should be interviewed, though there might be as 
many as six worth interviewing. 
 
The anticipated interview group included Maggie Herlihy, Jeff Horan, Joey Pellegrino, Kelly Curran, plus Vice 
Chairperson Moriarty participating if available.  Chairperson Horan stated an intent to review applicants on 
Monday August 17th with the hope of conducting interviews the following week.  recommended that the interview 
group confer after the application deadline regarding scheduling and interview questions, with the goal of 
reviewing applicants during the week of August 17 and completing interviews as quickly as practical during the 
following week.
Page 5 of 6 
 
 
The Chair also reported that Joey Pellegrino would begin work the following Monday.  To allow an overlap period 
between Mr. Pellegrino and Ms. Herlihy, Ms. Herlihy had agreed to return temporarily to the Conservation Planner 
position.  Commissioners expressed appreciation for that arrangement.  Ms. Herlihy stated that the transition was 
bittersweet but that she was grateful the department would have approximately three weeks of overlap and hoped 
a new planner could be identified before her departure. 
 
8. Discussion – Conservation Commission Informal Gathering 
The Commission discussed arranging a lunch or dinner to recognize Ms. Herlihy before her last day.  After 
discussing availability, the penciled-in date was Wednesday, September 2nd.  The back-up date was chosen as 
Friday, September 4th.  as a backup.  Members discussed possible Holyoke restaurants as the meeting place but did 
not finalize all the details. 
 
9. Formal Vote – Minutes from 5/14/26 Meeting 
Ms. Herlihy reported that a draft of the May 14 meeting minutes had been received from InfraWare and placed in 
the Google Drive for review.  She stated that the turnaround had been very quick and that she would review the 
draft against the recording, correct names and any substantive issues, and have the minutes ready for 
consideration at the August 27 meeting.  She also planned to submit additional recordings so that the backlog of 
minutes could be reduced. 
 
Staff explained that the transcription/minutes service was believed to be approximately $150 per meeting hour 
and that a blanket purchase order of approximately $4,000 to $5,000 had been established to cover the 
outsourcing expenses.  No minutes were formally approved. 
 
10. Discussion – Upcoming Items for 8/27/26 Meeting 
Ms. Herlihy advised that the August 27 agenda was expected to include the 5 Appleton Street continuance and the 
Notice of Intent for 500 Easthampton Road continuance.  The 500 Easthampton Road applicant remained in 
coordination with Natural Heritage and might need an additional continuance depending on the status of that 
review. 
 
Ms. Herlihy also reported that MassDEP was seeking suggested webinar topics.  Commissioners were invited to 
identify subjects such as enforcement orders or site visits that would be useful for future training.   
 
Chairperson Horan reported meeting with Ms. Herlihy and Mike Gallagher from Public Works regarding 
implementation of the Mayor’s urban forestry and tree pit executive order and stated that the departments were 
working toward a coordinated plan.  
 
11. Mail/other items not reasonably anticipated by the Chair 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty noted the Department's new goals about education, and suggested a City Hall coffee 
hour to introduce the new agent and planner to be part of that agenda.  She also offered a tour for Mr. Pellegrino of 
Holyoke's water resources among other things which had been given to various Conservation Commission 
members in the past.
Page 6 of 6 
 
 
12. Adjourn 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty moved to adjourn.  The meeting was adjourned at approximately 8:11 p.m.
